Save a CONSORT diagram for manuscript submission

Source: R/export.R
save_consort_diagram.Rd

Writes a CONSORT flow diagram to a PNG, TIFF, JPEG, PDF, SVG or EPS file via ggplot2::ggsave(), with defaults suited to journal submission: 300 dpi raster output, a white background, and a page size derived from the diagram's layout so that box text fits its boxes.

Usage

save_consort_diagram(
  diagram,
  path,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  units = c("in", "cm", "mm", "px"),
  dpi = 300,
  ...
)

Arguments

diagram

A consort_diagram from as_consort_diagram(), or a cf_flow, which is drawn with as_consort_diagram(diagram)'s defaults. Build the diagram yourself to customise it.

path

File to write. The extension (.png, .tiff/.tif, .jpeg/.jpg, .pdf, .svg or .eps, case-insensitive) picks the format.

width, height

Plot size in units. NULL (default) derives it from the diagram layout; see Details.

units

Units of width and height: "in", "cm", "mm" or "px".

dpi

Resolution for raster formats. Default 300.

...

Further arguments passed to ggplot2::ggsave(), e.g. bg = "transparent" (the default background is "white") or device = to override the device choice.

Value

path, invisibly.

Details

The file format is chosen from the extension of path. PNG, TIFF and JPEG use the ragg devices when that package is installed (sharper, anti-aliased text), otherwise the base grDevices::png() family. PDF uses grDevices::cairo_pdf() when R has cairo support, which embeds fonts (so a custom font_family renders correctly), otherwise grDevices::pdf(). SVG uses svglite::svglite() when installed, otherwise grDevices::svg().

When width and height are both NULL, the size is taken from the diagram's layout so that text_size-point text fills its boxes, scaled up proportionally for larger text_size. A longer pipeline therefore produces a taller file. Supply only one of width / height to fix it and keep the diagram's aspect ratio. Text is always drawn at text_size points, so a size much smaller than the natural one will overflow the boxes and a much larger one leaves them sparse. To fit a wide diagram (e.g. a two-arm trial) on the page, build it with a smaller text_size in as_consort_diagram(); the natural size shrinks in proportion.

See also

as_consort_diagram()

Other reporting: as_attrition_table(), as_attrition_tibble(), as_characteristics_table(), as_characteristics_tibble(), as_consort_diagram()

Examples

dat  <- mock_parallel_rct(n_participants = 200, seed = 1)
crit <- cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ !is.na(age), label = "Age recorded") |>
  include(~ age >= 18,   label = "Adults only") |>
  exclude(~ withdrew,    label = "Withdrew consent")
flow <- apply_criteria(dat, crit)
#> No `id` supplied and no `.cf_row_id` column found. Adding a sequential `.cf_row_id`.

png_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
save_consort_diagram(flow, png_file)

pdf_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")
diagram <- as_consort_diagram(flow, title = "Participant flow")
save_consort_diagram(diagram, pdf_file, width = 6)
unlink(c(png_file, pdf_file))
